Q Does the v2ecoli baseline single-cell→division ensemble reproduce the basal-condition physiology of glucose-minimal MG1655 — growth rate, biomass yield, glucose uptake, central-carbon fluxes, exchange rates, proteome census, macromolecular composition, and metabolite pools — when graded against curated experimental + theoretical reference values rather than a pinned run?

Claim

Does the v2ecoli baseline single-cell→division ensemble reproduce the basal-condition physiology of glucose-minimal MG1655 — growth rate, biomass yield, glucose uptake, central-carbon fluxes, exchange rates, proteome census, macromolecular composition, and metabolite pools — when graded against curated experimental + theoretical reference values rather than a pinned run?

Test

Model population_phenotype_basal
Measures growth-rate-in-band·glucose-uptake-below-band·biomass-yield-first-principles-violation

Result

The baseline ensemble makes 0.826 gDW of biomass per gram of glucose consumed — 1.86× the top of the measured band (0.355–0.444) and 1.54× the first-principles ceiling of 0.538. No carbon- and energy-balanced cell can exceed that ceiling, so this is a model defect, not a calibration mismatch. The dispersion is tight (CV 1.55% across 20 cells), so it is a systematic property of the model rather than noise. Carbon is nonetheless conserved at baseline — implied biomass carbon ≈ 0.457 gC/gDW is physically plausible — which locates the defect on the energetic side: the ensemble barely respires (O₂:glucose ≈ 0.09, CO₂:glucose ≈ 0.33, RQ ≈ 3.6 against ~1 for full oxidation), so almost no glucose carbon is burned for maintenance and ATP, and nearly all of it is retained as biomass.

×0.8598 vs expected
expected: [0.355, 0.444] · threshold: 0.538 ·
Reference says: Measured band 0.355–0.444 gDW/g glucose from four aerobic glucose-minimal determinations — varma_1994 (0.355, W3110 aerobic batch), kavvas_2022 (0.42, ¹³C-MFA MG1655), lacroix_2015 (0.44, MG1655 M9), long_2017 (0.444, ¹³C-MFA MG1655). The threshold is the first-principles ceiling, varma_1993 = 0.538 (FBA, fully aerobic, no maintenance energy); a value above it is forbidden by carbon and energy balance rather than merely unusual.
→ Next: Re-measure Yxs on a fresh basal run whose commit is recorded, and compute carbon closure and RQ on the same run, to establish whether the baseline defect is energetic and distinct from the carbon creation seen under a binding uptake cap. Tracked as study metabolism-biomass-yield-s1-diagnostic.
